page: Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-300s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core, alongside 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 16.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX, AES-NI, SHA-NI, and BMI2 instruction sets, though extended vector formats like AVX-512 and matrix extensions are omitted. Local high-speed persistence is integrated via a 300 GB NVMe solid-state drive.

Benchmark measurements indicate pronounced single-threaded efficiency paired with standard multi-threaded capacity. In single-core tests, the server achieved a stress-ng score of 3213.28, placing it in the top decile, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 2122.0. Multi-threaded metrics align across mid-tier percentiles, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core result of 25653.07, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 10810.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 19815.41. Large-block memory throughput reaches 118.62 GB/sec for reads and 68.98 GB/sec for writes. In application-level benchmarks, Redis sustained 16.48 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measured 9.2 GB/sec. Lightweight language model execution yields 240.07 tokens per second on 135M parameter models, but larger 7B models show constrained prompt processing at 25.18 tokens per second.

Resource allocation provides balanced compute capability with fast attached storage, though memory density remains low per core. This profile aligns with build environments, CI/CD runners, batch processing, static web serving, and database nodes that do not exceed the 16 GB memory threshold.
description: Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor at 2.0 GHz. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a compute-optimized 2 GB per core ratio, alongside a local 300 GB NVMe solid-state drive. Hardware capabilities include hardware-accelerated AES and SHA cryptographic instructions with standard AVX extensions. Synthetic benchmarks highlight strong single-core performance, ranking in the upper tiers of stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth settle near median cloud averages. Application metrics show stable throughput across Redis operations and static web delivery, though larger language model processing is constrained by core memory limits. This server is structured for compute-bound tasks, CI/CD automation, code compilation, and transactional services requiring direct NVMe local storage without vast memory footprints.
